compiled_state.description:
## Why
rebar's mutating verbs follow the Unix rule of silence: `link`, `unlink`, `comment`, `tag`, `edit`, `set-file-impact` exit 0 with empty stdout on success. Observed cost (2026-08-14, bug clubby-circular-halicore): success and silent idempotent no-op are indistinguishable on stdout, so agents run a second `rebar show` per mutation to verify their own write; one agent misread silent success as failure, filed a spurious bug, and retried. Modern CLI practice (clig.dev; kubectl/git/gh/terraform) confirms every state change on stdout; the confirmation belongs in the mutation's own output.

## Scope
- **IN**: `_WRITES_FULL` (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:125) + `_LIFECYCLE` (:114). Verbs that already print — `create`, `idea`, `revert`, `claim`, `session-log`, `transition` (emits `UNBLOCKED: ...` transition.py:628, `Reverted event ...` :463, though not the from->to itself) — are NORMALIZED to the same message contract (operator-approved 2026-08-14): the line keeps every datum it prints today (ids/aliases are consumed by scripts — no information loss) restated in the step-1 style, e.g. `created <alias> (<id>)`, `claimed <alias>: open -> in_progress (assignee <who>)`, Old->new mappings documented in the change + regenerated cli-reference.
- **OUT**: MCP tools (outputSchemas already confirm), doctor/fsck/compact/bridge/tracker-maintenance (own reporting), config-key equivalent of --quiet.

## Plan
1. **Uniform message contract.** Success: one stdout line `<past-tense-verb> <args-summary>` built only from CLI args + the seam's outcome (no follow-up store read): `linked <src> -> <target> (<relation>)`, `unlinked <src> -/-> <target> (<relation>)`, `comment added to <alias>`, `tagged <alias>: +<tag>`, `untagged <alias>: -<tag>`, `edited <alias>: <field-names>` (comma-joined names of fields the invocation set, e.g. `edited x: description, priority` — names only, never values), `impact set on <alias>: <n> paths`, `archived <alias>`, `verify-commands set on <alias>: <n>`, `commits attached to <alias>: <n>`, `reopened <alias>: closed -> open`. transition's normalized line is `transitioned <alias>: <from> -> <to>; unblocked: <ids|none>` — the UNBLOCKED datum is preserved inside the line, not dropped. No-op (where the seam reports one): `no change: <specific reason>` — e.g. `no change: already linked <src> -> <target> (<relation>)`, `no change: tag <tag> already on <alias>`. Exit 0 both ways.
2. **Per-verb outcome signal, existing contracts preserved.** Confirm each core seam's ACTUAL return contract before touching it (Serena + string grep), then extend compatibly:
   - Seams returning `None` with no consumers gain a small outcome return (wrote/noop + detail).
   - Seams whose return IS consumed — e.g. `add_dependency` returns `dict | None` (REDIRECT record), propagated by `link_core` and consumed by the MCP/library facade — are NOT changed; the CLI derives the confirmation from what the seam exposes, adding a parallel channel only if the existing signal cannot distinguish wrote-vs-noop, never altering the consumed value's type or meaning.
   - Verbs with no idempotent no-op path (e.g. `comment` always writes) get success lines only; an inventory table in the change classifies each verb.
3. **Global output flags pre-extracted at the top-level router** (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py) BEFORE any partition dispatch — required because the positional-only `_REGISTRY` leaf verbs (comment, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands — `_REGISTRY` is defined in src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:41, dispatched from the `_cli/__init__.py` router) treat any option-looking token as a usage error and never call parse_output. Pre-extraction strips BOTH global flags from argv once, uniformly for every verb (operator-approved 2026-08-14):
   - `--quiet`/`-q`: suppresses confirmation lines only; errors/exit codes untouched.
   - `--output <mode>`/`-o <mode>`: PROMOTED from per-verb parse_output handling to the same top-level extraction, so every in-scope verb (including `_REGISTRY` leaves) gains `--output json`. Verbs already accepting it keep identical behavior (same modes, same JSON shapes); newly-covered verbs emit ONE uniform mutation envelope — {"outcome": "<verb-past>"|"noop", "subject": <alias/edge>, "detail": <str>} (kubectl-Status-style; bespoke per-verb schemas are deliberately NOT designed here) — documented as pre-1.0-unstable in cli-reference. `--quiet` + `--output json` together: JSON still prints (quiet governs the text confirmation channel only).
   Extraction is position-independent but never consumes tokens after `--` or verb-argument values (tested: a comment body containing "--quiet" is preserved).
4. **Channel discipline:** confirmations print only in text mode. Under `--output json` stdout is exclusively the JSON document; the outcome rides as a structured field.
5. **REDIRECT reconciliation:** `link` already prints a machine-readable redirect record as raw JSON to stdout on write and no-op paths (`_emit_redirect`, src/rebar/graph/_links.py:220 — an existing CLI contract), PRESERVED byte-identical; when a redirect record is printed in text mode, no additional text confirmation line is added on top (one result on stdout per invocation, no mixed text+JSON). The record is MACHINE DATA, not a confirmation line: `--quiet` never suppresses it (quiet governs only the step-1 text lines), so `link --quiet` on a redirect path still emits the record byte-identical. Under --output json the record nests as an envelope field; golden tests pin both paths.
6. **stdout/stderr split:** confirmations to stdout (the command's result); warnings/logs stay on stderr. Exit codes unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Every verb in `_WRITES_FULL` + `_LIFECYCLE` that is silent today prints the step-1 success line on a successful write (edit's line lists exactly the field names passed on that invocation, no values); per-verb tests assert the exact line and that no additional store read/reduce builds it (call-count or monkeypatch assertion on the reduce path).
- [x] Every verb whose seam reports an idempotent no-op prints the `no change: ...` form, exits 0, writes no event (store-event count asserted); the change includes the inventory table classifying each verb (no-op-capable vs always-writes), and re-link of an identical active edge is among the tested no-ops.
- [x] Already-printing verbs (create, idea, revert, claim, session-log, transition) are normalized to the shared contract with zero information loss: for each, a test asserts the new line contains every datum the old line carried, and the change description lists each old->new mapping. reopen (silent today) gains a step-1 line.
- [x] link's REDIRECT record emission is byte-identical before/after on write and no-op paths, including under `--quiet` (golden tests); in text mode a redirect invocation prints exactly one stdout result (the record, no extra confirmation line).
- [x] transition's normalized line preserves the UNBLOCKED ids datum (test: close-with-unblock asserts ids present in the new line).
- [x] Consumed seam returns are unchanged: `add_dependency`'s `dict | None` REDIRECT contract and its `link_core`/facade consumers verified untouched by tests that exercise the REDIRECT path.
- [x] `--quiet`/`-q` AND `--output json` work on every in-scope verb including the positional-only `_REGISTRY` leaves (tested on at least comment + tag), quiet suppressing only the confirmation; under `--output json` stdout stays a single valid JSON document with the outcome field; verbs with existing --output support keep byte-identical JSON shapes (golden tests); extraction never consumes tokens after `--` or option-lookalike verb-argument values (tested with a comment body containing "--quiet").
- [x] Confirmations on stdout, logs on stderr (captured-stream tests); existing exit-code contract tests stay green.
- [x] docs/user-guide.md + cli-reference regenerated; `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
